quote: A system, based on Project Debater, for generating morally-framed arguments.
we extend the capabilities of Project Debater ... to generate morally-framed arguments.
This work studies the feasibility of generating morally framed arguments computationally and the effect of these arguments on different audiences.
outputs: Arguments with specific moral framing (care, fairness, loyalty, authority, purity)

quote: we let selected participants rank the different arguments on specific controversial issues based on how effective they were in challenging or empowering the audience's stance; and ... two authors of this paper manually assessed the quality of the generated arguments and ranked their relevance, coherence, and argumentativeness on a 5-point Likert scale.
we conducted a user study with two opposing target audiences, liberals and conservatives ... participants rank the different arguments ... by perceived effectiveness.
To evaluate our hypothesis on the effect of morally framed arguments, we carried out a user study with two opposing target audiences, liberals and conservatives.
guideline: Participants ranked arguments by effectiveness (challenging or empowering); authors rated relevance, coherence, and argumentativeness using a 5-point Likert scale.
participants read each set of arguments and ranked them according to perceived effectiveness (empowering or challenging)

For each pair, the participants read the three arguments and ranked them by perceived effectiveness, defined as how empowering it is (if the participant has the same stance) or how challenging it is (otherwise).
